+# HEIDENHAIN TNC dialects by NC software version
+
+Research notes for the CamCraft HEIDENHAIN posts (`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` for DIN/ISO, `assets/posts/heidenhain-klartext.cps` for Klartext). The notes tell which words, cycles and cycle parameters each HEIDENHAIN control accepts, and from which NC software version. They do not change code.
+
+Collected in November 2026.
+
+## Files
+
+| File | Content |
+|---|---|
+| [`dialects.md`](dialects.md) | Proposal: `controller.identity` values, capability flags, profiles (control + NC software → flags), what each post must branch on, what the posts assume today |
+| [`differences.md`](differences.md) | A: the common language of all controls. B: what the oldest manual of each series adds. B2: post-relevant features with "introduced / changed / removed" and references. B3: Q-parameter lists of cycles 200, 203, 205, 207 and 209 by version |
+| [`differences-by-version.md`](differences-by-version.md) | Section C: per control, each NC software version in release order, with the entries of its new-function list (generated, short pointers only) |
+| [`cycles.md`](cycles.md) | Each cycle number in these notes: HEIDENHAIN name, purpose, DIN/ISO code, software option, versions, reference |
+| [`inventory.md`](inventory.md) | Each manual used: control, NC software, title, HEIDENHAIN ID, edition date, pages, download URL; the overview documents; dead links |
+| [`picomax-55-review.md`](picomax-55-review.md) | Review of the two HEIDENHAIN posts and the machine file `fehlmann-picomax55.mch` against the Fehlmann programming manual and the machine parameters (MP) of a Picomax 55 with iTNC 530 340490-03 |
+
+## Method
+
+1. The source is the public HEIDENHAIN TNCguide portal: the English user manuals of 6 series, 15 control models and 84 NC software pages (TNC 124 to TNC7), plus the "Overview of New and Modified Software Functions" documents and some brochures. `inventory.md` lists each document.
+2. The text of each PDF was extracted with `pdftotext -layout`. Scripts searched the text. Nobody read the manuals page by page.
+3. The main sources are the "New functions" / "Changed functions" lists of each manual and the overview documents. The Q-parameter lists of the cycles come from the example block that starts with the cycle's own number and name (section B3 of `differences.md`).
+4. Section C assigns an entry to a control only when the manual covers that control. The DIN/ISO manual 345 940-22 is shared by the TNC 410, TNC 426 and TNC 430. Its "not TNC 410" marks were applied, so its 280 476 list counts for the TNC 426/430 only.
+5. Short excerpts were read to confirm a detail. Each fact has a document ID and a PDF page (`<ID> p<N>`).
+6. A gap is marked "unsure" or "not found in the extracted text". "Not found" does not prove that a control lacks a function.
+
+## How complete
+
+- All six series of the portal are covered. Every manual with a new-function list was processed: iTNC 530 340 420 to 60642x-04 SP8, TNC 320, TNC 620, TNC 640, TNC7 and TNC 128.
+- The old manuals without such lists (TNC 124, TNC 310, TNC 410, TNC 426/430) are covered by keyword search only. The TNC 426 280 460 manual is a scan without text and was not analysed.
+- The TNC 406 / TNC 416 are EDM controls. They are out of scope.
+- Three portal links are dead (HTTP 404). Three brochures were blocked (HTTP 403). The most useful missing document is "Functions of the TNC7".
+
+## Copyright and clean-room note
+
+The HEIDENHAIN manuals are © HEIDENHAIN. These files hold facts about control behaviour with document references. They do not hold manual text, except short phrases with the document ID and the page. No manual and no extracted text is in this repository. Use the URLs in `inventory.md` to get a manual. HEIDENHAIN manuals are allowed reference material for behaviour facts (AGENTS.md, "Clean-Room Protocol"). No HSMWorks material was used.
+
+## Top findings for the posts
+
+1. **Three dialect groups.** TNC 124 and TNC 128 are paraxial: one axis in each block, no `L`, no arcs, `R+`/`R-`. TNC 310 is contouring Klartext only. All other controls add DIN/ISO from a version on.
+2. **DIN/ISO is not on all controls.** None on TNC 310, TNC 128 and TNC 124. TNC 320 from 340 55x-04, TNC 620 from 340 56x-02, TNC 426/430 from 280 472, TNC7 only from 81762x-17.
+3. **Cycle 205 (UNIVERSAL PECKING) grew in steps.** Q379/Q253 from iTNC 340 422. Q208 and Q395 only from iTNC 60642x-04, TNC 640 34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01 and TNC 320 77185x-01 (1096959-20 p9). Cycle 200 (DRILLING) has Q395 from the same releases. The TNC 426/430 gets cycle 205 only from 280 474. The TNC 410 has no cycle 205. The DIN/ISO post writes Q395/Q208 today, so its output is not valid on iTNC 530 340 49x software (#4094).
+4. **`FUNCTION DWELL` is on no iTNC 530 version.** It comes with TNC 640 34059x-07, TNC 620 81760x-04 and TNC 320 77185x-04. Use `G04 F..` (cycle 9 DWELL TIME) in DIN/ISO (#4093).
+5. **Cycle 247 (PRESETTING) changed meaning in iTNC 340 422.** Before, it set a datum value. After, it activates a row of the preset table.
+6. **PLANE** comes with iTNC 340 422, TNC 620 340 56x-02 and TNC 320 340 55x-04. PLANE AXIAL comes with iTNC 34049x-03. The TNC7 keeps cycle 19 (WORKING PLANE) only to edit old programs (from 81762x-17), and converts cycle 7 (DATUM SHIFT) into TRANS DATUM.
+7. **FUNCTION TCPM in ISO programs** comes only with TNC 640 34059x-10 and TNC 620 81760x-07. Before that, and on the iTNC 530 ISO side, use M128. The TNC 320 has no 5-axis option.
+8. **Tool calls.** The tool name in quotes comes with TNC 426 280 462 (not TNC 410 or TNC 310). The name length went from 16 to 32 characters in TNC 640 34059x-02. FZ/FU come with iTNC 34049x-01. TNC7 81762x-19 refuses `L`/`R` in `TOOL DEF`.
+9. **Options.** On the TNC 620, cycles 201-205, 208 and 209 need option 19. Tilting needs option 8 and TCPM needs option 9. The existing `installed_options` field can carry this.
+10. **Number format.** TNC 310, TNC 410 and TNC 124 take 1 µm (3 decimals). TNC 426/430, iTNC 530, TNC 320/620/640 and TNC7 take 0.1 µm (4 decimals). TNC 640 34059x-11 changed the operator priority in Q formulas: write parentheses.
+11. **TNC 410.** The shared ISO manual 345 940-22 marks cycles 205-209, 247, 19 (G80), 32 (G62), the SL II cycles, M128 and the tilted working plane as "not TNC 410". The TNC 410 profile in `dialects.md` follows these marks.
+
+## Related issues
+
+- #4095: the HEIDENHAIN posts write the dialect of the control and NC software in the machine file. `dialects.md` is the proposal for it.
+- #4093: `FUNCTION DWELL` in DIN/ISO (finding 4).
+- #4094: Q395 and Q208 in cycles 200/205 (finding 3).
+- #4085, #4086, #4087, #4088: defects from the Picomax 55 review (tool change without a stop, arc tolerance, tool numbers above 254, preset row 6).
+- #3095: verify the DIN/ISO output on a real iTNC 530 340490-03.

+# HEIDENHAIN cycle numbers: names, purposes and versions
+
+This table lists every HEIDENHAIN cycle number that occurs in these notes (`differences.md`, `differences-by-version.md`, `dialects.md` and the script output, which is not published), plus the touch probe cycles of the same families. Use it to read a bare number such as "205" as "205 UNIVERSAL PECKING".
+
+## How this table was made
+
+- **Names** come from the cycle headings and cycle overview tables of the HEIDENHAIN English user manuals. A script searched the extracted manual text for the form `Cycle <n> <NAME> (ISO: G<n>)` and for the section headings of each cycle. No manual was read in full.
+- The **name** column gives the short name of the newest manual (TNC7 81762x-20 where the cycle exists there), then older or long forms in parentheses. The control shows the short form in the `CYCL DEF` block.
+- The **purpose** column is written in our own words. It is not HEIDENHAIN text.
+- **DIN/ISO** is the G code of the cycle in DIN/ISO programs. "(none found)" means that no G code was found in the extracted text.
+- **Option** is the software option number that the TNC 620 (`620: #19`), TNC 640 or TNC7 manuals name for the cycle. On the iTNC 530, TNC 320 and TNC 640, option 19 functions are standard. Turning cycles need the turning option (#50) on the TNC 640 and TNC7.
+- **In example blocks** comes from `CYCL DEF <n>` lines in the manuals of each version (script output, the cycle list per version). "320 340 551-01 on" means: seen from 340 551-01 to the newest manual of that control. "A to B" means: seen from A to B, not in the newer manuals. "only" means: seen in one version only. The list shows where an example block exists. It does not prove that a version without an example block lacks the cycle. Gaps inside a range are not shown.
+- **Introduced / changed / removed** gives the facts of sections B2, B3 and C of `differences.md`. "C names it: ..." lists the versions whose new-function or changed-function list names the cycle (generated; read the bullet in section C for the detail).
+- **Reference** is the HEIDENHAIN manual ID and the PDF page (not the printed page) of the cycle heading or of the contents line that was used. `inventory.md` maps each ID to the control, the NC software, the title and the download URL.
+
+Control abbreviations: 128 = TNC 128, 310 = TNC 310, 320 = TNC 320, 410 = TNC 410, 426/430 = TNC 426 / TNC 430, iTNC = iTNC 530, 620 = TNC 620, 640 = TNC 640, TNC7 = TNC7.
+
+Cycle families in short:
+
+- **1-5, 17, 18**: old fixed cycles with `CYCL DEF n.0` ... `n.x` blocks and no Q parameters.
+- **6, 14, 15, 16**: SL I contour cycles (TNC 410 era). **14, 20-25, 270, 271-277**: SL II and OCM contour cycles.
+- **7, 8, 10, 11, 26, 19, 247**: coordinate transformations and presets. **9, 12, 13, 32**: special cycles.
+- **200-299**: Q-parameter machining cycles. **800-899**: turning cycles. **1000-1099**: grinding cycles. **1271-1282**: OCM standard figures.
+- **TCH PROBE 0-4, 400-499, 1400-1499**: touch probe cycles. **600/601**: camera monitoring cycles. These run as `TCH PROBE n` blocks, not `CYCL DEF n`.
+
+## Numbers that are not cycles
+
+The script list of cycle numbers per version also contains numbers that are not HEIDENHAIN cycles. They are extraction artefacts:
+
+- **140**: `CYCL DEF 14.0 CONTOUR GEOMETRY` read without the point (cycle 14).
+- **42, 56, 60, 66, 68, 70, 72, 84, 94, 242**: block numbers or page numbers next to a `CYCL DEF` line. No cycle with these numbers was found in the manuals.
+- **G122, G124, G125** and similar in section C are the DIN/ISO codes of cycles 22, 24 and 25.
+- The TNC 406 / TNC 416 numbers (1, 3, 7, 8, 10-12, 14, 16, 17, 19 in the script list) are EDM cycles. They are out of scope and are not explained here.
+
+## Names marked unsure
+
+- **202**: the TNC7 81762x-20 manual heading reads "Cycle 202 REAMING" (1358775-24 p207). All other manuals, the G code and the cycle text give BORING. We use BORING.
+- **1051 STEP. CYLIND. GRIND** and **1040 END CYLIND. GRINDING**: only the short form was found; the long name and the exact purpose are unsure.
+- **18 THREAD CUTTING**: one TNC 640 manual prints the ISO code as G18 (1303406-20). G18 is the plane code; we use G86.
+- Options marked "(unsure)" were not found next to the cycle heading.
+

+# Proposal: how CamCraft models HEIDENHAIN dialects
+
+Source facts: `differences.md` (sections B2 and B3 hold the version thresholds used below). Status: proposal only. It does not change code.
+
+Cycle numbers: the first bare number in each section has its HEIDENHAIN short name in parentheses. `cycles.md` has the full table.
+
+## 1. What the machine file states
+
+CamCraft already has the right field (#3181, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` lines 299-305 on `origin/main`):
+
+```json
+"controller": {
+  "post": "Heidenhain Klartext",
+  "identity": { "model": "iTNC 530", "nc_software": "340490-03", "installed_options": ["1", "19"] }
+}
+```
+
+Recommendation: **add no new machine-file field.** The file keeps stating facts only (control model, NC software, options). The post derives the dialect from these facts. This follows the existing rule "The file states facts only. Each post decides which documented releases and operations it serves."
+
+Make the values canonical, so that one resolver can read them:
+
+| Field | Canonical form | Examples |
+|---|---|---|
+| `model` | the model name as HEIDENHAIN writes it | `TNC 124`, `TNC 128`, `TNC 310`, `TNC 320`, `TNC 410`, `TNC 426`, `TNC 430`, `iTNC 530`, `TNC 620`, `TNC 640`, `TNC7`, `TNC7 basic` |
+| `nc_software` | 6-digit ID, `-`, 2-digit release, optional ` SP<n>` | `340490-03`, `606425-04`, `606425-04 SP8`, `817600-18`, `340595-11`, `771851-18`, `817625-20` |
+| `installed_options` | HEIDENHAIN option numbers as strings | `"8"` (Advanced Function Set 1: tilting/PLANE, rotary table), `"9"` (Advanced Function Set 2: FUNCTION TCPM / M128 5-axis), `"19"` (Extended programming functions: FK, cycles 201-205/208/209 on TNC 620), `"23"` (0.01 µm display step). The iTNC 530 uses the older numbers `"1"` (tilting) and `"2"` (5-axis) for the same functions. |
+
+The resolver reads the family from the first five digits and the last digit as the variant: `34049` + `0..4` = iTNC 530 single/dual processor; `60642` + `0..5` = iTNC 530 HSCI line; `34056`/`73498`/`81760` = TNC 620; `34059` = TNC 640 (all releases -01 to -18); `34055`/`77185` = TNC 320; `77184` = TNC 128; `81762` = TNC7 (TNC7, TNC7 basic and TNC7 go share it, so key the resolver on `(model, nc_software)`). The release number (`-03`) orders versions inside one family. The iTNC 530 order is: 340420 < 340422 < 34049x-01 ... -05 < 60642x-01 (= 34049x-06 functions) < -02 (= -07) < -03 (= -08) < -04 < -04 SP8.
+

+# HEIDENHAIN TNC: differences between controls and NC software versions (post-processor view)
+
+Sources: the HEIDENHAIN manuals and overview documents listed in `inventory.md` (document ID, title, edition date, download URL). The manuals themselves are not in this repository.
+
+**How this file was made (read this first).**
+
+- The manuals were not read page by page. The text was extracted with `pdftotext -layout` and searched with scripts. The main source is the "New functions" / "Changed functions" lists at the front of each manual, and the "Overview of New and Modified Software Functions" documents (TNC 620 ID 1322094, TNC 640 ID 1322095, TNC7 ID 1373081 / 1465689). Only short excerpts of the full chapters were read, to confirm a detail.
+- The Q-parameter lists of cycles (section B3) come from the example blocks in the manuals. A script takes the block that starts with the cycle's own number and name (`CYCL DEF 205 UNIVERSAL PECKING`, `N110 G205 UNIVERSAL PECKING`) and collects the `Qnnn=` lines up to the next NC block. The first version of B3 searched for the bare number and took the longest list near any match; it mixed in other cycles (for example the G220 pattern parameters in the iTNC cycle 200 rows). B3 was made again with the new rule. A row was kept only when its list starts with Q200 and ends at the next NC block or at the end of the example. Rows were spot-checked against the PDF pages. B3 covers 200, 203, 205, 207 and 209 only.
+- References: `<manual ID> p<N>` means the PDF page N of that manual. "printed p" means the page number printed in the manual. A version written as `34049x-05` means all variants (340490/340491/340492/340493/340494-05). The iTNC 530 340 49x numbers and 606 42x numbers run in parallel: 606 42x-01 follows 340 49x-05 (single-processor/HSCI line), and 340 49x-06..-08 have the same functions as 606 42x-01..-03 (the 34049x-08 manual lists "60642x-01 since the predecessor version 34049x-05").
+- "not found in the extracted text" means a keyword search found nothing. It does not prove that the control lacks the function.
+- Section C is in its own file, `differences-by-version.md`. It is generated from the new/changed-function lists. A bullet is "post-relevant" when it names a post-dialect keyword (TOOL CALL, PLANE, TCPM, M-functions, cycles 1-32/200-247, ISO, Q/QS parameters, FMAX/FZ/FU, arcs/helix, program names, removed/import notes). All other bullets are cut to one short line under "other". Some bullets are cut off in the middle where the PDF column layout broke them; follow the manual ID and page.
+- Cycle names: the first bare cycle number in each section of sections A, B, B2 and B3 has its HEIDENHAIN short name in parentheses, for example "205 (UNIVERSAL PECKING)". `cycles.md` has the full table (name, purpose, DIN/ISO code, option, versions).
+- "feature-mentions.md" in a source column means a keyword search of the extracted text (which keywords appear in which version's manuals). That matrix is not published here. It is evidence for a search, not proof of support.

+## A. Standard library (all covered controls)
+
+The covered controls do not share one dialect. Three groups exist:
+
+1. **Positioning displays / straight-cut controls (TNC 124, TNC 128).** Each positioning block holds ONE axis. There is no `L` word, no circle and no DIN/ISO. Radius compensation is `R+` / `R-` (lengthen or shorten a paraxial move) or `R0`.
+   - TNC 124 (246 xxx-08, 284 679-24 p72): `BEGIN PGM 10 MM` (program NUMBER), `F 9999`, `Z+20`, `X-20 R0`, `TOOL CALL 1 Z`, `S 1000`, `M 3`, `CYCL 1.0 PECKING` ... `CYCL 1.7 F 80`, `CYCL CALL`, `END PGM 10 MM`. Max 1000 NC blocks per program, 2000 in total (p? "2000 NC blocks. A single program can contain a maximum of 1000", 284 679-24, line 3222 of the text).
+   - TNC 128 (77184x, 819494-26 printed p132): `BEGIN PGM LINEAR MM`, `BLK FORM 0.1/0.2`, `TOOL CALL 1 Z S4000`, `Z+250 R0 FMAX`, `X+5 R- F500`, `CYCL DEF 200 ...` with Q-parameters, M99. It has the 200-series drilling cycles, 247, 251-256, FN functions and QS strings, but no arcs.
+2. **Contouring controls, Klartext only (TNC 310).**
+3. **Contouring controls with Klartext and (from a version on) DIN/ISO (TNC 410, TNC 426/430, iTNC 530, TNC 320, TNC 620, TNC 640, TNC7).**
+
+**Common to ALL controls (groups 1-3):** `BEGIN PGM <name|number> MM|INCH` ... `END PGM <same> MM|INCH`; numbered blocks (the control numbers them); `TOOL CALL <n> Z` (tool number, spindle axis); F, S and M words; `R0`; `FMAX` (TNC 124 uses `F 9999` instead); `CYCL DEF` / `CYCL CALL`; M3/M4/M5, M8/M9, M2/M30 (by the standard M list of each manual).
+
+**Common to all CONTOURING controls (TNC 310 and later) - the practical "standard library" for CamCraft:**
+
+| Element | Form | Evidence (oldest manual of the group) |
+|---|---|---|
+| Program frame | `BEGIN PGM NAME MM` / `END PGM NAME MM` | TNC 310 313 509-22 p43 |
+| Blank | `BLK FORM 0.1 Z X.. Y.. Z..` / `BLK FORM 0.2 X.. Y.. Z..` | 313 509-22 p45 |

+# HEIDENHAIN TNC manuals: inventory
+
+Collected 2026-11-26 from the HEIDENHAIN TNCguide portal (`https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/html/en/index/1242135142456/1242135142456.html`, portal edition "TNCguide (10/2026)"). English editions only. Programming manuals only: Klartext / conversational, DIN/ISO, cycles (machining and measuring), setup, and the "Overview of New and Modified Software Functions" documents. Not downloaded on purpose: other languages, smarT.NC pilots, training courses, CHM help archives, TNC7 "complete edition" PDFs, TNCdiag, machine-parameter overviews, NC error message lists.
+
+The manuals were downloaded once (about 3.5 GB) for text extraction with `pdftotext -layout`. They are not part of this repository. Use the source URL to get a manual.
+
+**Terms:** the portal pages show only "© HEIDENHAIN 2026" and link "Conditions of Use" to `http://www.heidenhain.de/de_EN/company/terms-of-use/`. That page (and heidenhain.com) answered HTTP 403 to automated requests, so the terms were not read. The PDFs carry HEIDENHAIN copyright. Use them as behaviour facts only; quote short phrases with page numbers.
+
+Column "date" is the most frequent `mm/yyyy` in the manual text (normally the edition date in the page footer). "pages" is the PDF page count. Page numbers elsewhere in these notes are PDF pages unless the text says "printed page".

+# Fehlmann Picomax 55 / HEIDENHAIN: review of CamCraft's two HEIDENHAIN posts and the machine file
+
+> Published copy of a review made for CamCraft issue work (#3095, #4085-#4088). The machine data come from the machine's parameter backup on its delivery CD. Access codes, passwords and file names that identify the single machine are removed. The MP numbers and values are kept. Line numbers such as `heidenhain.cps:381` refer to `origin/main` at commit `034e91b8b`.
+
+- CamCraft checked at `origin/main` `034e91b8b` (read through git, nothing checked out or changed).
+- Manual: Fehlmann "PICOMAX 55 CNC 2/3 Programming manual", P07-35-06-E (2006), 340 pages.
+  Page references look like "p. 2-19 (PDF 47)". The first number is the page number printed in the manual. The PDF number is the page in the PDF file.
+- **Machine data (added later):** the machine's parameter backup from its delivery CD (the MP file). Header: "Maschinenparameter für P55CNC mit iTNC530 (MC422(B)/UV106B) · ID 340490 03 · W. FEHLMANN AG · Stand 1.11.07". The review also used `OEM.SYS`, `PRESET.PR` and the PLC file list (LST file) from the same backup, and the machine owner's notes. Machine parameters are cited as "MP nnnn". The access codes and passwords in these files are left out. **See section 4a.**
+- Files reviewed: `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` (DIN/ISO), `assets/posts/heidenhain-klartext.cps` (Klartext), `assets/machines/fehlmann-picomax55.mch`, the Heidenhain goldens and recorded goldens, `crates/app/tests/klartext_builtin.rs`, issue #3095 and the follow-up notes on #3095.
+
+**About the manual.** This manual does not name the control model or the NC software version. It also does not give travel, spindle or feed limits. It says those are in the operating and maintenance manual, chapter 7 (p. 1-5, PDF 13). The MP file fills these gaps. **Every example in the manual is Klartext. There is no DIN/ISO example anywhere in it.** DIN/ISO files are still allowed on this control (MP 7224, section 4a).
+
+---
+
+## 1. Summary
+
+- **Klartext post:** safe and careful, but narrow. It covers milling only: flat, ball, bull-nose and chamfer cutters, straight moves and flat XY arcs, one setup per program. It refuses all drilling and tapping, helices, smoothing and stops between operations. Its arc check is 160 times stricter than the control (MP 7431 = 0.016 mm). It works for single-setup 2.5D/3D milling jobs. It cannot post a complete part that has holes.
+- **DIN/ISO post:** much wider. It has drilling, peck and tap cycles (G200/G205/G206/G207), presets, XZ/YZ arcs as short lines, setup-change stops and smoothing. The control allows `.I` files (MP 7224). It was tested on a programming station (606425-04, #3095), **not yet on the real Fehlmann (340490-03)**. It knows nothing about this machine's **manual tool change** (see defect 1).
+- **Machine file:** consistent with the machine parameters. Spindle 9000 rpm in one gear range, rapids 11000/11000/6000 mm/min, iTNC 530 340490-03, manual change, flood M8. Missing: travel limits (X 0..500.2, Y 0..255.2, Z -147.2..0), max feed, rigid tapping (yes), the M92 change position and the tool-table size (254).
+- **Top 5 to fix:**
+  1. DIN/ISO on the Picomax: the tool call has no retract and no stop. The next tool's length becomes active while the old tool is still in the spindle. Refuse the post on a manual-change machine, or add the Fehlmann sequence. M6 halts the program on this machine (MP 7440 bit 0 = 0), so `M6` is a correct stop.
+  2. Check the DIN/ISO output on the real 340490-03 control: Q395 (G200/G205), Q379/Q253 (G205) and `FUNCTION DWELL TIME`. The 2006 software probably does not know them. For the dwell, use G04.
+  3. Klartext: add drilling and tapping cycles 200/205/207, and drill/tap tool kinds. This is the biggest gap for everyday work. Rigid tapping works on this machine (MP 7160 bit 2).
+  4. Klartext arc check: use the control's tolerance, MP 7431 = 0.016 mm, not 0.0001 mm. Limit tool numbers to 1..254 (MP 7260) in both posts.
+  5. Tool change and program end in the Fehlmann way: `L Z+0 R0 FMAX M92` (MP 950: the change height), an XY park move, then M6 or M0. Put the MP values into the machine file (section 4a).
+
+---
+

+## 5. DIN/ISO vs Klartext
+
+- **What the manual and the control expect:** Klartext. The whole manual is conversational, and the machine file names Klartext. **DIN/ISO is allowed** on this control: MP 7224 locks no file type, and MP 7220 sets the DIN block-number step (10). The open point is only which words the 340490-03 software accepts (defects 2, 3).
+
+| Area | DIN/ISO (`heidenhain.cps`) | Klartext (`heidenhain-klartext.cps`) |
+|---|---|---|
+| Program frame | `%name G71 *` … `N99999999 %name G71 *` | `BEGIN PGM … MM` … `END PGM` |
+| Blank form | none | BLK FORM 0.1/0.2 |
+| Machine/control guard | none (any 3-axis machine) | strict: Picomax, iTNC 530, 340490-03, XYZ only, manual change |
+| Tool change | T block only, no stop (defect 1) | M0 with operator checks, M140 MB MAX, checks |
+| Tool numbers | no limit | 1..32767 (control: 254) |
+| Preset | `G247 Q339=n` (1-6) | `CYCL DEF 247` Q339 (1-6) |
+| Drilling/tapping | G200, G205, G206, G207, and expanded ream/back-bore | refused |
+| Arcs | XY with absolute I/J; XZ/YZ as short lines; helix refused | XY `CC`/`C` only, with a 0.0001 mm check (control: 0.016) |
+| Cutter compensation | refused | refused |
+| Coolant | flood/mist/air/through, from the machine list | flood only |
+| Stops between ops, setup change | yes | refused |
+| Smoothing | `G62 T..` | refused |
+| Probing, inch, rotary | refused | refused |
+| Tested on a control | station 606425-04 (#3095) | not yet on a control |
